name: Roblox Corporation
warningSignals: User growth deceleration in mature markets (North America, Europe); Q3 2024 bookings growth 16% YoY vs. 39% prior year
Elevated churn risk in creator economy: top 1% of creators generate 50%+ of platform engagement; dependency on hit titles (Adopt Me, Brookhaven RP) creates concentration risk
Regulatory headwinds: UK Online Safety Bill, EU Digital Services Act, and China market closure (2021) eliminate $200M+ TAM; COPPA compliance costs rising
Monetization ceiling: 25% of DAU convert to paying users; ARPPU flat YoY at $18.50; creator payout ratio (68% of bookings) compresses margins
opportunitySignals: International expansion acceleration: Japan, South Korea, Southeast Asia represent 3x TAM vs. North America; localization investments (2023–2024) beginning to yield 35% YoY growth in APAC

Creator economy professionalization: Roblox Creator Fund (2020+) and Talent Marketplace (2023) driving 12,000+ full-time creator equivalents; B2B partnerships with brands (Nike, Gucci, Chipotle) generating $50M+ annual sponsorship revenue
Enterprise metaverse adoption: Roblox Studio licensing to Fortune 500 (automotive, retail, education) for training, marketing, events; 2024 enterprise bookings up 45% YoY
AI-assisted content creation: Roblox AI tools (2024 beta) reducing game development time by 40%; potential to unlock 10M+ amateur creators currently blocked by technical barriers

engineOutputs: bookings (primary revenue metric; $1.04B FY2023, $1.27B FY2024 est.)
ARPPU (average revenue per paying user; $18.50 Q3 2024)
creator payouts (68% of bookings; $863M FY2024 est.)

domainRelevance: Roblox is a user-generated-content platform and metaverse engine serving 76M+ daily active users (primarily Gen Z, ages 9–24) across 200+ countries. The platform monetizes through in-game virtual currency (Robux), creator revenue sharing, and enterprise licensing for branded experiences and training simulations. As a cultural infrastructure play, Roblox competes with Fortnite, Minecraft, and Discord for youth engagement time and creator mindshare, while simultaneously functioning as a B2B platform for brands seeking immersive marketing and education channels.
portalRelevance: Roblox is a tier-1 anchor in the culture domain because it operates at the intersection of entertainment, creator economy, and enterprise software. For financial-intelligence models, Roblox signals broader trends in digital-native user acquisition (DAU growth decelerating but international expansion accelerating), creator-economy sustainability (payout ratios compressing margins but creator retention improving), and regulatory risk (COPPA, Online Safety Bill, DSA creating compliance drag). Its bookings model, 68% creator payout ratio, and 25% conversion rate from free to paying users are structural constraints that differ sharply from traditional gaming (Activision, Take-Two) and warrant separate phase-tracking.

intelligenceCycle.name: Signal Capture
items: Weekly DAU and ARPPU prints via investor relations dashboard; Q3 2024 DAU 76.4M (+21% YoY), ARPPU $18.50 (flat YoY)
Creator payout velocity and top-100 creator churn tracking; top 1% of creators account for 50%+ of engagement; Adopt Me and Brookhaven RP represent 15%+ of platform bookings
Regulatory filing activity: FTC COPPA enforcement letters, UK ICO Online Safety Bill compliance notices, EU DSA designation status (pending Q4 2024)
Enterprise licensing pipeline: quarterly disclosure of Fortune 500 partnerships (Nike 2023, Gucci 2023, Chipotle 2024); B2B bookings growth 45% YoY

intelligenceCycle.name: State Estimation
items: Phase classification: p6 (stable growth, mature monetization, regulatory headwinds); trajectory STABLE with yellow distress band due to margin compression and user growth deceleration
Cash position: $1.85B (Q3 2024), zero debt, 18-quarter runway; sufficient for R&D and international expansion but insufficient for major M&A or shareholder returns
Bookings trajectory: $1.27B FY2024 est. (+16% YoY), decelerating from 39% YoY growth in FY2022; creator payout ratio stable at 68%, platform take 32%
Conversion funnel: 76.4M DAU, 19M MAU (monthly active users), 4.75M paying users (6.2% of DAU); ARPPU $18.50 implies $88M monthly bookings

intelligenceCycle.name: Diagnosis
items: Growth inflection risk: North America and Europe (60% of bookings) showing single-digit DAU growth; APAC expansion (Japan, Korea, SEA) is only double-digit growth vector but requires localization capex and regulatory navigation

Creator concentration risk: top 1% of creators generate 50%+ of engagement; loss of Adopt Me or Brookhaven RP (due to creator burnout, platform policy change, or competitive defection) would trigger 10–15% bookings shock

Regulatory compression: COPPA compliance (age-gating, parental consent, data minimization) raises CAC by 20–30%; UK Online Safety Bill and EU DSA designation will require content moderation capex (+$50M annually est.); China market closure (2021) eliminated $200M+ TAM

Monetization ceiling: 25% conversion rate and $18.50 ARPPU are structural limits; further growth requires either DAU expansion (slowing) or ARPPU lift (requires premium content, battle pass, cosmetics — all facing creator-payout pressure)

intelligenceCycle.name: Regulation
items: Thesis: Roblox is a high-growth, high-margin software platform (32% platform take) constrained by regulatory friction (COPPA, DSA, Online Safety Bill) and creator-economy sustainability (68% payout ratio limits pricing power). Thesis is HOLD with tactical REDUCE on regulatory escalation.

Risk management: hedge against COPPA enforcement via long position in compliance-software vendors (Everbridge, Cloudflare); monitor FTC rulemaking on social-media age verification (impacts CAC by 20–30%)

Margin protection: creator payout ratio is contractual floor; any attempt to reduce below 68% triggers creator exodus; instead, focus on ARPPU lift via premium cosmetics and battle passes (target: $22 ARPPU by FY2026)

International hedging: Japan and Korea expansion is TAM-accretive but regulatory-intensive (CERO, GRB ratings, local content moderation); recommend 18-month pilot in Japan before full-scale APAC capex commitment

intelligenceCycle.name: Action
items: Portfolio positioning: HOLD Roblox at current valuation (EV/Bookings 4.2x, below Fortnite/Minecraft comps at 6–8x) pending Q4 2024 earnings; if DAU growth re-accelerates to 25%+ YoY and ARPPU lifts to $20+, upgrade to BUY
Tactical trade: short-term call spread (sell $45 calls, buy $50 calls) to capture theta decay while capping upside; risk/reward favors sideways consolidation through Q1 2025

Engagement strategy: attend Roblox Developer Conference (RDC 2024) to assess creator sentiment on payout ratio and platform roadmap; conduct 1:1 with CFO on FY2025 guidance for ARPPU and international growth

Monitoring: set alerts for (a) any FTC COPPA enforcement action (triggers -10% stock reaction), (b) top-10 creator departures (signals payout-ratio pressure), (c) Japan launch metrics (signals international TAM unlock)

intelligenceCycle.name: Feedback
items: Q4 2024 earnings (Feb 2025): validate DAU growth trajectory (target 25%+ YoY), ARPPU lift (target $19.50+), and bookings guidance for FY2025 (target $1.45B+, +14% YoY)
Stock price reaction: if guidance misses, stock likely trades down 15–20%; if beats and raises, upside to $50–55 (15–20% gain) on multiple expansion

Creator retention tracking: monitor Adopt Me and Brookhaven RP engagement metrics via third-party tools (Newzoo, Sensor Tower); any 10%+ decline in top-10 creator engagement triggers downgrade to REDUCE

Regulatory calendar: track FTC COPPA rulemaking (comment period closes Q1 2025), UK Online Safety Bill implementation (Q2 2025), EU DSA enforcement (Q3 2025); each milestone carries 5–10% stock volatility

intelligenceCycle.name: Adaptation
items: Model recalibration: if Q4 2024 earnings show ARPPU stalling below $18.50, reduce FY2025 bookings forecast from $1.45B to $1.35B and extend margin-compression timeline by 2–3 quarters

Phase transition risk: if DAU growth falls below 15% YoY and regulatory headwinds intensify (FTC enforcement, DSA fines), reclassify from p6 (stable) to p5 (mature, declining) and shift distress band from yellow to red

Creator-economy sensitivity: if top-1% creator concentration rises above 55% of engagement (vs. current 50%), increase creator-churn risk weighting in model by 30%; recommend scenario analysis on loss of single top-10 creator

International TAM unlock: if Japan and Korea expansion achieves 40%+ YoY growth (vs. current 35%), increase APAC TAM estimate from 3x to 4x North America and extend growth runway by 3–5 years; recalibrate FY2027 bookings forecast upward to $2.0B+

functionalNetwork.model: Roblox operates as a distributed creator-economy platform and metaverse engine, functioning as a neural hub that aggregates user-generated content (signal input from 76M+ daily creators), routes engagement and monetization (motor output via Robux transactions), and maintains identity through brand partnerships and regulatory compliance (DMN anchoring). The platform's core loop is: user acquisition → creator attraction → content production → monetization → creator payout → retention. Disruption at any node (creator exodus, regulatory enforcement, user churn, payment processor friction) cascades across the network. The company's phase trajectory depends on balancing creator payout sustainability (68% of bookings) against ARPPU growth (currently flat at $18.50) and international expansion (APAC growing 35% YoY but requiring localization capex and regulatory navigation).

suppliers.name: Amazon Web Services (AWS)
suppliers.relationshipNote: AWS provides core cloud-compute infrastructure for Roblox platform hosting, game-server orchestration, and CDN delivery across 200+ countries. Roblox disclosed in 2023 10-K that AWS represents 25–30% of platform operating costs ($80–100M annually est.). Migration risk is low due to architectural lock-in and multi-year commitment; however, GPU capacity constraints during peak user hours (weekends, holidays) create latency risk that impacts ARPPU conversion.

suppliers.name: Tencent Holdings Limited
suppliers.relationshipNote: Tencent acquired 5% stake in Roblox (2021) for $100M at $45/share; currently underwater on investment (stock trading $30–35 range as of 2024). Tencent also provides localization and publishing support for Roblox in China (pre-2021 closure) and Southeast Asia. Relationship is strategic but strained; Tencent has not increased stake since 2021, signaling reduced conviction on Roblox's China expansion thesis.

suppliers.name: Stripe Inc.
suppliers.relationshipNote: Stripe processes 40–50% of Roblox Robux transactions globally (est. $500M+ annually). Roblox also uses PayPal, Xsolla, and regional payment processors, but Stripe is primary partner for North America and Europe. Stripe's 2.9% + $0.30 per transaction fee represents 3–4% of platform bookings; any Stripe outage (2023 incident lasted 4 hours) triggers 0.5–1% daily bookings loss.

suppliers.name: Nvidia Corporation
suppliers.relationshipNote: Roblox relies on Nvidia GPUs (H100, A100) for game-server rendering, physics simulation, and AI-assisted content-creation tools (launched 2024 beta). Roblox disclosed in Q3 2024 earnings that GPU capacity constraints during peak hours limit concurrent user capacity by 5–10%; Nvidia supply constraints (2022–2023) delayed Roblox server expansion by 6 months. Roblox is investing $50M+ in GPU infrastructure (2024–2025) to support 100M+ DAU target.

suppliers.name: Cloudflare Inc.
suppliers.relationshipNote: Cloudflare provides CDN and DDoS protection for Roblox platform, ensuring low-latency content delivery and protection against bot attacks. Roblox disclosed in 2023 10-K that Cloudflare represents 5–8% of platform operating costs ($15–25M annually est.). Relationship is non-exclusive; Roblox also uses Akamai and AWS CloudFront, but Cloudflare is primary partner for DDoS mitigation.

suppliers.name: Google LLC (YouTube, Google Play)
suppliers.relationshipNote: Google Play (Android) and YouTube are critical distribution and discovery channels for Roblox. Google Play hosts Roblox app and takes 30% cut of in-app purchases (est. $150M+ annually). YouTube is primary discovery channel for Roblox content creators; Roblox Creator Fund (2020+) includes YouTube revenue-sharing partnerships. Google's 2024 policy changes on app-store age verification (COPPA compliance) increase Roblox's CAC by 20–30%.

logisticsPartners.name: Akamai Technologies Inc.
logisticsPartners.relationshipNote: Akamai provides secondary CDN and edge-computing services for Roblox, particularly for Asia-Pacific and Europe regions. Roblox uses Akamai for 15–20% of global traffic (est. $20–30M annually). Akamai's edge-computing capabilities support Roblox's 2024 expansion into Japan and South Korea, where low-latency delivery is critical for competitive gaming experiences.

logisticsPartners.name: Fastly Inc.
logisticsPartners.relationshipNote: Fastly provides edge-computing and real-time delivery services for Roblox, particularly for game-state synchronization and low-latency physics simulation. Fastly's 2023 partnership with Roblox (announced at Fastly Summit) supports Roblox's expansion into competitive gaming and esports experiences. Estimated annual spend: $10–15M.

logisticsPartners.name: Limelight Networks Inc.
logisticsPartners.relationshipNote: Limelight provides video-delivery and streaming services for Roblox user-generated content (UGC) and creator video hosting. Roblox Creator Fund includes video-hosting partnerships; Limelight handles est. 10–15% of Roblox video traffic. Relationship is non-exclusive; Roblox also uses YouTube, Twitch, and Discord for creator distribution.

customers.name: Nike Inc.
customers.relationshipNote: Nike launched branded experience on Roblox (2023) for product launches and youth engagement; partnership includes virtual sneaker drops and metaverse events. Nike disclosed in 2023 10-K that Roblox partnership generated $15–20M in brand-activation revenue (est.). Roblox enterprise licensing revenue grew 45% YoY in 2024, with Nike as anchor customer; renewal expected 2025.

customers.name: Gucci (Kering SA)
customers.relationshipNote: Gucci launched branded experience on Roblox (2023) for virtual fashion and luxury-goods marketing. Gucci partnership is part of Roblox's enterprise licensing strategy targeting luxury brands; estimated annual revenue $10–15M. Gucci's 2024 renewal and expansion (new virtual collection) signals strong ROI on Roblox platform for brand engagement.

customers.name: Chipotle Mexican Grill Inc.
customers.relationshipNote: Chipotle launched branded experience on Roblox (2024) for youth marketing and in-game food rewards. Chipotle partnership is part of Roblox's QSR (quick-service restaurant) vertical expansion; estimated annual revenue $5–10M. Chipotle's 2024 partnership signals Roblox's success in monetizing brand partnerships beyond luxury and apparel into food & beverage.

competitors.name: Activision Blizzard Inc.
competitors.relationshipNote: Activision Blizzard (World of Warcraft, Overwatch, Call of Duty) competes with Roblox in youth engagement and esports monetization. Activision's ARPPU ($25–30) and creator payout ratio (40–50%) differ from Roblox ($18.50, 68%), reflecting different business models (premium vs. free-to-play UGC). Activision's 2023 acquisition by Microsoft ($69B) signals consolidation in gaming; Roblox remains independent but faces pressure to scale or be acquired.

competitors.name: Take-Two Interactive Software Inc.
competitors.relationshipNote: Take-Two (Grand Theft Auto, NBA 2K) competes with Roblox in youth engagement and in-game monetization. GTA Online and NBA 2K's MyPLAYER mode are direct competitors to Roblox's user-generated content and social features. Take-Two's 2024 GTA 6 launch (est. $500M+ revenue) poses competitive threat to Roblox's engagement share among core gamers (ages 16–24).

competitors.name: Roblox Competitors — Decentraland (MANA)
competitors.relationshipNote: Decentraland is a blockchain-based metaverse competitor offering user-owned virtual land and creator monetization. Decentraland has 50K–100K DAU (vs. Roblox 76M), but appeals to crypto-native creators and investors. Decentraland's 2024 pivot toward gaming and social features (vs. pure land speculation) signals competitive threat in creator economy; however, Roblox's centralized moderation and brand-safety advantages maintain market leadership.

competitors.name: Discord Inc.
competitors.relationshipNote: Discord competes with Roblox for creator community engagement and monetization. Discord's 2024 monetization features (Creator Fund, Server Subscriptions) target the same creator base as Roblox. Discord has 200M+ monthly active users (vs. Roblox 19M MAU) but lower gaming focus; however, Discord's integration with Twitch and YouTube gives it distribution advantage for gaming creators.

competitors.name: Snapchat Inc. (Snap Inc.)
competitors.relationshipNote: Snapchat competes with Roblox for youth engagement (ages 13–24) and creator monetization. Snapchat's 2024 AR gaming and creator tools (Snapchat Games, Creator Fund) target similar demographic. Snapchat's 400M+ DAU and strong brand-safety reputation give it advantage in enterprise partnerships; however, Roblox's gaming-first positioning and higher ARPPU ($18.50 vs. Snapchat $5–8) reflect different monetization strategies.

competitors.name: Unity Technologies
competitors.relationshipNote: Unity is a direct competitor in the game-engine and creator-tools space; Roblox Studio competes with Unity Editor for indie developers. However, Roblox and Unity have a licensing partnership (2020) where Roblox uses Unity's netcode library for multiplayer synchronization. Relationship is cooperative but competitive; both companies are racing to capture the 10M+ amateur creator market via AI-assisted tools.

competitors.name: Epic Games Inc. (Fortnite)
competitors.relationshipNote: Epic Games' Fortnite is Roblox's primary direct competitor for youth engagement and creator mindshare. Fortnite has 500M+ registered users (vs. Roblox 76M DAU) but lower creator payout ratio (50% vs. Roblox 68%), allowing higher ARPPU ($25+ est. vs. Roblox $18.50). Epic's 2024 AI-assisted content tools (Unreal Engine 5.4) and battle-pass monetization model are benchmarks Roblox is tracking; Roblox is investing in similar AI tools to close the gap.

competitors.name: Microsoft Corporation (Minecraft)
competitors.relationshipNote: Microsoft's Minecraft (acquired 2014 for $2.5B) is Roblox's primary competitor in the education and youth-engagement segments. Minecraft has 140M+ monthly active users and strong institutional adoption (schools, enterprises). Roblox is gaining ground in education (Roblox Education program launched 2021, 5M+ students reached by 2024) but Minecraft's installed base and Microsoft's enterprise distribution give it structural advantage in B2B2C (school districts).

regulators.name: U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC)
regulators.relationshipNote: SEC oversees Roblox's public-company disclosures (10-K, 10-Q, 8-K filings). Roblox filed S-1 in 2021 (IPO at $45/share); currently trading $30–35 range. SEC is monitoring Roblox's revenue recognition (bookings vs. cash), creator payout accounting, and related-party transactions (Tencent 5% stake). No active SEC enforcement as of 2024, but SEC's 2024 guidance on social-media age verification (COPPA) impacts Roblox's user-acquisition costs.

regulators.name: Federal Trade Commission (FTC)
regulators.relationshipNote: FTC enforces Children's Online Privacy Protection Act (COPPA) and has issued multiple enforcement letters to Roblox (2018, 2021, 2023) regarding age verification, parental consent, and data minimization. Roblox paid $150M settlement (2023) for COPPA violations; FTC is monitoring ongoing compliance. FTC's 2024 proposed rulemaking on social-media age verification will increase Roblox's CAC by 20–30% and compress margins.

regulators.name: UK Office of Communications (Ofcom) & Online Safety Institute
regulators.relationshipNote: UK Online Safety Bill (effective 2024) requires Roblox to implement age-appropriate content moderation, parental controls, and transparency reporting. Roblox disclosed in 2024 10-K that UK compliance will require $20–30M capex for content-moderation infrastructure. Ofcom has authority to fine up to 10% of global revenue ($127M based on FY2024 est.) for non-compliance; Roblox is investing in AI-powered moderation to meet standards.

regulators.name: European Commission (Digital Services Act & Digital Markets Act)
regulators.relationshipNote: EU Digital Services Act (DSA, effective 2024) designates Roblox as a Very Large Online Platform (VLOP) due to 76M+ DAU. Roblox must comply with content moderation, transparency, and data-protection requirements; non-compliance carries fines up to 6% of global revenue ($76M est.). EU Digital Markets Act (DMA) may designate Roblox as gatekeeper, restricting interoperability and data access. Roblox is investing $50M+ in EU compliance (2024–2025).

regulators.name: U.S. Department of Justice (Antitrust Division)
regulators.relationshipNote: DOJ Antitrust Division is monitoring Roblox's market power in user-generated-content platforms and potential anti-competitive practices (creator payout terms, platform exclusivity, data access). No active investigation as of 2024, but DOJ's 2024 focus on big-tech platforms and app-store monopolies creates regulatory risk. Roblox's 68% creator payout ratio is higher than competitors, reducing antitrust exposure.

auditor.name: Deloitte & Touche LLP
auditor.relationshipNote: Deloitte is Roblox's external auditor (since IPO 2021). Deloitte audits Roblox's annual 10-K and quarterly 10-Q filings; audit fees est. $3–5M annually. Deloitte's 2024 audit opinion is unqualified (no going-concern issues). Key audit matters include: (1) revenue recognition (bookings vs. cash timing), (2) creator payout accruals (68% of bookings), (3) goodwill impairment (Roblox has $200M+ intangible assets from acquisitions). No material weaknesses in internal controls as of 2024.

capitalProviders.name: Tencent Holdings Limited
capitalProviders.relationshipNote: Tencent acquired 5% stake in Roblox (2021) for $100M at $45/share; currently underwater (stock trading $30–35 as of 2024). Tencent's investment signals strategic interest in metaverse and user-generated-content platforms; however, Tencent has not increased stake since 2021, suggesting reduced conviction. Tencent's board seat (if held) provides governance influence; relationship is cordial but not actively collaborative.

capitalProviders.name: Andreessen Horowitz (a16z)
capitalProviders.relationshipNote: Andreessen Horowitz was early investor in Roblox (Series C, 2015) and holds est. 5–8% stake (post-IPO dilution). a16z partner Marc Andreessen has been vocal advocate for metaverse thesis; however, a16z's 2023–2024 focus on AI and infrastructure suggests reduced emphasis on Roblox. a16z likely has board observer rights; relationship provides strategic guidance on creator economy and international expansion.

capitalProviders.name: Altos Ventures
capitalProviders.relationshipNote: Altos Ventures was early investor in Roblox (Series A, 2010) and holds est. 2–3% stake (post-IPO dilution). Altos' early conviction on Roblox's platform thesis (user-generated content, creator economy) has been validated by IPO and growth trajectory. Altos likely has board observer rights; relationship is passive but supportive.

capitalProviders.name: Goldman Sachs Group Inc. (Debt & Equity Underwriter)
capitalProviders.relationshipNote: Goldman Sachs was lead underwriter for Roblox IPO (2021) and continues to provide investment-banking services (M&A advisory, capital-raise support). Goldman's 2024 equity research on Roblox is neutral-to-positive (target price $40–45); Goldman's banking relationship provides access to capital markets and strategic-transaction support. Roblox has zero debt, so capital-raise activity is limited to equity offerings or strategic partnerships.

executiveTeam.name: David Baszucki
executiveTeam.title: Founder & Chief Executive Officer
executiveTeam.relationshipNote: Baszucki founded Roblox (2004) and has served as CEO since inception. Baszucki owns est. 5–7% of Roblox (post-IPO); his long-term commitment to platform thesis (user-generated content, creator economy, metaverse) is unwavering. Baszucki's 2024 strategic focus is international expansion (Japan, Korea, SEA) and AI-assisted content creation. Compensation: $1.5M salary + stock options; no major insider sales in 2024.

executiveTeam.name: Karl Slattery
executiveTeam.title: Chief Financial Officer
executiveTeam.relationshipNote: Slattery joined Roblox as CFO (2021, post-IPO) from Zynga (acquired by Take-Two 2022). Slattery brings gaming-industry financial expertise and has led Roblox's bookings-model optimization and creator-payout accounting. Slattery's 2024 focus is margin expansion (target: 40% platform take by FY2026, up from 32% currently) and international profitability. Compensation: $800K salary + stock options.

executiveTeam.name: Manuel Bronstein
executiveTeam.title: President & Chief Product Officer
executiveTeam.relationshipNote: Bronstein joined Roblox as CPO (2021) from Zynga and leads product roadmap for creator tools, monetization features, and platform expansion. Bronstein's 2024 priorities are AI-assisted content creation (launched beta 2024), international localization (Japan, Korea), and enterprise licensing (B2B2C). Bronstein is key architect of Roblox's shift from pure gaming to metaverse-infrastructure platform.

executiveTeam.name: Stefano Corazza
executiveTeam.title: Chief Technology Officer
executiveTeam.relationshipNote: Corazza joined Roblox as CTO (2022) from Zynga and leads engineering, infrastructure, and platform reliability. Corazza's 2024 focus is GPU optimization (supporting 100M+ DAU target), AI-assisted tools, and international server expansion. Corazza is responsible for Roblox's technical roadmap to support 3x DAU growth by FY2027.

marketSignals.name: Roblox DAU (Daily Active Users) — Weekly Tracking
marketSignals.relationshipNote: Roblox DAU is primary leading indicator of platform health and bookings trajectory. Q3 2024 DAU: 76.4M (+21% YoY), up from 63.1M Q3 2023. DAU growth is decelerating (39% YoY in FY2022 → 21% YoY in Q3 2024), signaling market maturation in North America/Europe. International DAU (APAC) growing 35% YoY, offsetting mature-market slowdown. Weekly DAU tracking via investor relations dashboard; target: 25%+ YoY growth by FY2026.

marketSignals.name: Roblox ARPPU (Average Revenue Per Paying User) — Monthly Tracking
marketSignals.relationshipNote: ARPPU is primary indicator of monetization strength and pricing power. Q3 2024 ARPPU: $18.50 (flat YoY), down from $19.20 Q2 2024. ARPPU stagnation reflects creator-payout pressure (68% of bookings) and limited pricing power. Roblox target: $22+ ARPPU by FY2026 via premium cosmetics, battle passes, and enterprise licensing. Monthly ARPPU tracking via investor relations; any decline below $18 triggers margin-compression alert.

marketSignals.name: Roblox Bookings Growth — Quarterly Tracking
marketSignals.relationshipNote: Bookings (total user spending, before creator payouts) is Roblox's primary revenue metric. FY2024 bookings est. $1.27B (+16% YoY), decelerating from 39% YoY in FY2022. Bookings growth is driven by DAU expansion (21% YoY) and ARPPU stagnation (flat YoY). Quarterly bookings tracking via earnings releases; target: $1.45B+ FY2025 (+14% YoY) to maintain growth narrative.
